guide.title: How Fleet Setup works
guide.subtitle: Connect → domain TLS → subscribe VIN → stream on wake.

step1.title: Connect Tesla
step1.body: Sign in with Tesla OAuth. TeslaSync stores a refresh token and renews the access token automatically — you should not paste tokens by hand.

step2.title: Point Tesla at this host
step2.body: Fleet Telemetry needs a public hostname with a TLS certificate Tesla trusts (Let’s Encrypt is the default CA). Partner registration also publishes your EC public key at /.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem.

step3.title: Subscribe the vehicle
step3.body: Call Tesla’s fleet_telemetry_config for the selected VIN. That tells the car (via Tesla) where to stream, which signals to send, and which CA to trust for your server.

step4.title: Wait for the car to wake
step4.body: Streaming starts when the vehicle is awake — usually the next drive or charge. Parked and asleep cars will not push telemetry. Virtual key pairing is for commands, not this stream.

connect.title: Connect Tesla account
connect.body: Authorize TeslaSync. The refresh token stays on the server and is renewed automatically.

token.title: Keep the Fleet token fresh
token.body: A valid access token is required for subscribe. TeslaSync refreshes it in the background.

subscribe.title: Subscribe telemetry
subscribe.body: Tell Tesla which VIN should stream to this host. Empty host/CA uses FLEET_TELEMETRY_HOST and Let’s Encrypt.

stream.title: Confirm streaming
stream.body: The car must be awake. First packets usually arrive on the next drive or charge session.

readiness.title: Domain & certificates
readiness.subtitle: Tesla verifies your telemetry host with TLS, and your partner key at a well-known URL.
readiness.body: Subscribe leaves hostname and CA empty on purpose: TeslaSync sends FLEET_TELEMETRY_HOST (port 4443) and the Let’s Encrypt root. Override those only if your telemetry endpoint uses a different certificate.
readiness.advancedBody: The well-known PEM is for Tesla partner registration and virtual-key pairing. Telemetry streaming does not wait on a phone key pair. Pairing is only required if you want TeslaSync to send vehicle commands.

subscribe.title: Subscribe telemetry
subscribe.subtitle: Pick signals (or a preset), then tell Tesla which VIN should stream to this host.
subscribe.signalsHint: Optional. Open the signal picker to choose fields and intervals. Leave empty to use TeslaSync’s default set.
subscribe.signalsPicked: {{count}} signals selected. Presets (Balanced, Low Power, Track Mode, …) set intervals per category.
subscribe.needAuth: Connect Tesla first. Subscribe uses the stored Fleet token.
subscribe.needVehicle: No vehicles yet. Sync vehicles after connecting Tesla.
subscribe.configEmpty: No fleet_telemetry_config on this VIN yet.
subscribe.pickHint: Pick a VIN to see whether Tesla already has a telemetry config for it.
subscribe.wakeHint: Wake the car so Tesla can apply the config. Asleep vehicles ignore fleet_telemetry_config until the next drive or charge.
subscribe.removeBody: Tesla will stop streaming this VIN to TeslaSync until you subscribe again.
subscribe.errorNoDetail: Tesla reported a telemetry error for this VIN.
subscribe.errorsEmpty: No Tesla-side telemetry errors for this VIN.
subscribe.advancedHint: Leave blank to use FLEET_TELEMETRY_HOST, port 4443, and the Let’s Encrypt root CA.

stream.title: Streaming
stream.subtitle: Fleet Telemetry only flows while the vehicle is awake.
stream.staleMessage: Telemetry was seen before, but nothing arrived in the last 24 hours. Wake the car or start a drive.
stream.waitingMessage: No stream yet. After subscribe, Tesla delivers the first batch when the vehicle next wakes.
stream.note: Virtual key pairing is not part of this step. Use it later if you want TeslaSync to send commands.
